q0AnchorReason: Reads no q0. The m = 6 R^{w_F} computation and its CGZ gates are exact 5-adic arithmetic over K = Q(alpha); the substrate modulus never enters.
source: CGZ arXiv:1712.04887v3 eqn (3), Lemma 2.4(b) even case, Lemma 2.4(c), Proposition 2.5; Addenda 33-37 (this repo)

result.verdict: m = 6 yields no independent datum: the 2-part of B^x/(B^x)^6 is killed by the even power w_F = 4 and the surviving 3-part is the m = 3 group, so R^{w_F} re-expresses the m = 3 invariant. Same collapse is expected at m = 12 and m = 24; m = 8 is the only structurally new live case.

scope: scope-(a) CROSS-CHECK, not a new invariant. m = 6 is the smallest live case where gcd(m, w_F) > 1, so Prop 2.5 defines only R_zeta(xi)^{w_F}. The mechanism carries over -- every unit of Z_5 is a 6th power in B = Q_25 (its Teichmueller part lies in mu_4 = (mu_24)^6), so H is not needed and the eqn-(21) ratio is a 6th power in B, giving root independence over all 36 choices. The four CGZ gates were re-run at m = 6 before any value was believed, including the five-term relation and both constructed-to-fail controls, and Lemma 2.4(b) in its EVEN form (D_zeta(1)^2 a root of unity). RESULT: R^{w_F} is computable but carries no information beyond m = 3 -- the 2-part of B^x/(B^x)^6 is killed by the even power w_F = 4 and the surviving 3-part is the m = 3 group. Measured symbol by symbol against a direct m = 3 computation, not argued from CRT. So m = 6 re-confirms Addenda 33-35 through a different m rather than adding a datum, and the same collapse is expected at m = 12 and 24, leaving m = 8 as the only structurally new live case. Nothing wired.
